problems.name: Assign Cookies
problems.question: Given children greed factors and cookie sizes, return the maximum number of children that can receive one cookie with size at least their greed.

examples.explanation: Only the child with greed 1 can be satisfied.
Cookies 1 and 2 satisfy both children.
Only greed 7 and 8 can be satisfied.

problems.optimizedComplexity: Time O(g log g + s log s); Space O(log g + log s) for sorting. Two pointers make each local match final.
problems.recursiveComplexity: Time O(g log g + s log s + g + s); Space O(log g + log s + g + s). Recursive two-pointer scan after sorting.

problems.name: Lemonade Change
problems.question: Customers pay in order with 5, 10, or 20 dollar bills for 5 dollar lemonade. Return true if exact change can be given to every customer.

examples.explanation: The 20 can be changed with 10 + 5.
The final 20 cannot be changed because no 5 remains.
There is no 5 dollar bill for change.

problems.optimizedComplexity: Time O(n); Space O(1). Keep only counts of 5 and 10 dollar bills.
problems.recursiveComplexity: Time O(n); Space O(n). Recursive scan applies the same safe change preference.

problems.name: Jump Game
problems.question: Given nums where nums[i] is the maximum jump length from index i, return true if the last index is reachable from index 0.

examples.explanation: The frontier reaches the final index.
The frontier stops at index 3.
The start is already the end.

problems.optimizedComplexity: Time O(n); Space O(1). Maintain the farthest reachable index.
problems.recursiveComplexity: Time O(n^2); Space O(n). Memoized recursion checks each index and possible jump once.

problems.name: Jump Game II
problems.question: Given nums where nums[i] is the maximum jump length from index i, return the minimum number of jumps needed to reach the last index.
problems.constraints: 1 <= nums.length <= 10000; 0 <= nums[i] <= 1000; the last index is reachable.

examples.explanation: Jump from index 0 to 1, then to the last index.
The same two-jump route works.
No jump is needed.

problems.optimizedComplexity: Time O(n); Space O(1). Greedy range expansion behaves like BFS levels over indexes.
problems.recursiveComplexity: Time O(n^2); Space O(n). Memoized recursion computes the minimum jumps from each index.

problems.name: Gas Station
problems.question: Given gas and cost arrays around a circular route, return the starting station index that can complete the circuit, or -1 if impossible.

examples.explanation: Starting at station 3 completes the circuit.
Total gas is less than total cost.
The single station has enough gas.

problems.optimizedComplexity: Time O(n); Space O(1). One pass tracks total surplus and the current candidate start.
problems.recursiveComplexity: Time O(n); Space O(n). Recursive scan applies the same reset rule.

problems.name: Candy
problems.question: Given children ratings in a line, give each child at least one candy and give higher-rated children more candies than adjacent lower-rated children. Return the minimum candies needed.

examples.explanation: Candies [2,1,2] satisfy both sides.
Candies [1,2,1] are enough.
The peak must exceed both neighboring slopes.

problems.optimizedComplexity: Time O(n); Space O(n). Two directional passes compute minimum local requirements.
problems.recursiveComplexity: Time O(n); Space O(n). Memoized recursion computes candy need from lower-rated neighbors.

problems.name: Queue Reconstruction by Height
problems.question: Given people as [height, k], reconstruct a queue where k is the number of people in front with height greater than or equal to height.

examples.explanation: Every person has exactly k taller-or-equal people before them.
Taller-first insertion preserves constraints.
A single person is already valid.

problems.optimizedComplexity: Time O(n^2 + n log n); Space O(n). Sorting is followed by list insertions.
problems.recursiveComplexity: Time O(n^2 + n log n); Space O(n). Recursively insert sorted people into the queue.

problems.name: Non-overlapping Intervals
problems.question: Given intervals, return the minimum number that must be removed so the remaining intervals do not overlap.

examples.explanation: Remove [1,3].
Only one identical interval can remain.
Intervals touching at endpoints do not overlap.

problems.optimizedComplexity: Time O(n log n); Space O(log n) for sorting. One end-time scan counts removals.
problems.recursiveComplexity: Time O(n log n + n); Space O(log n + n). Recursive scan after sorting by end time.

problems.name: Merge Intervals
problems.question: Given intervals, merge all overlapping intervals and return the non-overlapping result.

examples.explanation: [1,3] and [2,6] overlap.
Touching endpoints merge.
All intervals connect after sorting.

problems.optimizedComplexity: Time O(n log n); Space O(n). Sort by start and scan once.
problems.recursiveComplexity: Time O(n log n); Space O(n). Recursive scan appends or extends the last merged interval.

problems.name: Minimum Number of Arrows to Burst Balloons
problems.question: Given balloon intervals on the x-axis, return the minimum arrows needed; one arrow shot at x bursts every balloon containing x.

examples.explanation: Arrows at 6 and 12 can burst all balloons.
No intervals overlap.
An arrow at 2 bursts both.

problems.optimizedComplexity: Time O(n log n); Space O(log n) for sorting. One scan by right endpoint counts arrows.
problems.recursiveComplexity: Time O(n log n + n); Space O(log n + n). Recursive scan after sorting by right endpoint.

source.label: Minimum Number of Arrows to Burst Balloons - LeetCode 452

problems.name: Partition Labels
problems.question: Given a string, split it into as many parts as possible so each letter appears in at most one part. Return the sizes of the parts.
problems.constraints: 1 <= s.length <= 500; s contains lowercase English letters.

examples.explanation: Each letter appears in one partition only.
The characters force one full-string partition.
Each character can form its own partition.

problems.optimizedComplexity: Time O(n); Space O(1). Last occurrence array has fixed alphabet size.
problems.recursiveComplexity: Time O(n); Space O(n). Recursive segment builder uses last occurrences.

problems.name: Task Scheduler
problems.question: Given CPU tasks represented by letters and a cooldown n, return the least time units needed to execute all tasks with identical tasks separated by at least n intervals.
problems.constraints: 1 <= tasks.length <= 10000; tasks[i] is uppercase English letter; 0 <= n <= 100.

examples.explanation: One schedule is A B idle A B idle A B.
No cooldown means no idles.
The four A tasks create the limiting frame.

problems.optimizedComplexity: Time O(n + 26); Space O(26). Frequency formula computes the minimum frame length.
problems.recursiveComplexity: Time O(answer * 26); Space O(answer + 26). Recursive simulation chooses the most frequent available task each time.

problems.name: Reorganize String
problems.question: Given a string s, rearrange it so no two adjacent characters are equal, or return an empty string if impossible.
problems.constraints: 1 <= s.length <= 500; s contains lowercase English letters.

examples.explanation: The two a characters can be separated.
Three a characters cannot be separated by one b.
A valid arrangement separates repeated v characters.

problems.optimizedComplexity: Time O(n log 26); Space O(26). A max-heap chooses the highest remaining valid character.
problems.recursiveComplexity: Time O(n log 26); Space O(n + 26). Recursive heap construction places one character per call.

problems.name: Hand of Straights
problems.question: Given a hand of cards and groupSize, return true if the cards can be rearranged into groups of groupSize consecutive cards.

examples.explanation: The hand size is not divisible by 4.
Every card forms its own group.

problems.optimizedComplexity: Time O(n log n + n * groupSize); Space O(n). TreeMap keeps the next smallest card available.
problems.recursiveComplexity: Time O(n log n + n * groupSize); Space O(n). Recursive TreeMap removal builds one group at a time.

problems.name: Boats to Save People
problems.question: Given people weights and a boat limit where each boat carries at most two people, return the minimum number of boats needed.

examples.explanation: Both people fit in one boat.
The person with weight 3 rides alone.
No pair can include weight 5 or 4 with another person.

problems.optimizedComplexity: Time O(n log n); Space O(log n) for sorting. Two pointers pair lightest with heaviest when possible.
problems.recursiveComplexity: Time O(n log n + n); Space O(log n + n). Recursive two-pointer pairing after sorting.

problems.name: Two City Scheduling
problems.question: Given costs for flying each person to city A or B, send exactly n people to each city with minimum total cost.
problems.constraints: 2 <= costs.length <= 100; costs.length is even; 1 <= costA, costB <= 1000.

examples.explanation: Send people 0 and 1 to A, people 2 and 3 to B.
Sorting by savings gives the minimum split.
Exactly half must go to each city.

problems.optimizedComplexity: Time O(n log n); Space O(log n) for sorting. Difference sorting gives the exchange-optimal split.
problems.recursiveComplexity: Time O(n log n + n); Space O(log n + n). Recursive accumulation after sorting by cost difference.

problems.name: Maximum Subarray
problems.question: Given an integer array, return the largest possible sum of a non-empty contiguous subarray.

examples.explanation: The best subarray is [4,-1,2,1].
The single element is the answer.
The entire array has the maximum sum.

problems.optimizedComplexity: Time O(n); Space O(1). Kadane keeps only current ending sum and global best.
problems.recursiveComplexity: Time O(n log n); Space O(log n). Divide and conquer combines left, right, and crossing sums.

problems.name: Best Time to Buy and Sell Stock II
problems.question: Given daily stock prices, return the maximum profit with as many buy-sell transactions as desired, holding at most one share at a time.

examples.explanation: Profit 4 from 1->5 and 3 from 3->6.
Capture every adjacent increase.
No profitable transaction exists.

problems.optimizedComplexity: Time O(n); Space O(1). Sum every positive adjacent difference.
problems.recursiveComplexity: Time O(n); Space O(n). Recursive scan accumulates positive differences.

source.label: Best Time to Buy and Sell Stock II - LeetCode 122

problems.name: Can Place Flowers
problems.question: Given a flowerbed of 0s and 1s and an integer n, return true if n new flowers can be planted without adjacent flowers.
problems.constraints: 1 <= flowerbed.length <= 20000; flowerbed[i] is 0 or 1; 0 <= n <= flowerbed.length.

examples.explanation: Plant at index 2.
Only one new flower can fit.
The only plot has no neighbors.

problems.optimizedComplexity: Time O(n); Space O(1). One scan mutates valid empty plots.
problems.recursiveComplexity: Time O(n); Space O(n). Recursive scan applies the same earliest-placement rule.

problems.name: Increasing Triplet Subsequence
problems.question: Given an integer array, return true if there exists a strictly increasing subsequence of length three.

examples.explanation: 1, 2, 3 form a triplet.
No increasing subsequence of length three exists.
0, 4, 6 form a triplet.

problems.optimizedComplexity: Time O(n); Space O(1). Track the smallest first and second subsequence tails.
problems.recursiveComplexity: Time O(n); Space O(n). Recursive scan carries the two current tail values.
